name: Balinese gamelan gong kebyar (twentieth-century virtuosic gamelan)
lineage: Balinese gamelan gong kebyar Indonesian virtuosic gamelan ensemble form crystallizing in early-twentieth-century north Bali (Buleleng region) from the older gamelan gong gede court-ensemble form. The kebyar style is characterized by sudden dynamic-and-tempo contrasts (the term "kebyar" means "burst of flame"), virtuoso metallophone-player technique, and a more compressed performance duration suited to the post-colonial Balinese village-and-tourist performance economy. Performance configuration: ensemble of approximately 25-30 musicians playing tuned bronze metallophones (gangsa, ugal, jegogan, calung), gong chimes (reyong, trompong), kendang drums, and gong-cymbals. The annual Bali Arts Festival in Denpasar features kebyar competitions across all Bali regencies.
